newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW - NZ Dec qtr growth above forecasts.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - NZ Dec qtr growth above forecasts.

text.p: Following are economists' initial reactions to data on Thursday showing production-based New Zealand GDP rose 0.7 percent in the December 1996 quarter.
The median forecast had been for a 0.4 percent rise.
STEPHEN TOPLIS, DOYLE PATERSON BROWN ECONOMIST
"It's slightly larger than everyone expected, and that's about all you can say on first impressions.

"It's got the potential to have a modest negative (market) reaction, but I don't think anyone will get too carried away with it. It's historical, and people are more interested in what's happening now rather than last December. It's only
marginally at the top end of expectations."

Asked if the upward revision to September quarter growth, to 0.8 percent from 0.6 percent, had significance, Toplis said: "It does to the extent that if you believe the Reserve Bank's version, that the economy can only grow at 2.75 percent, then this tends to push it up above that in year-on-year growth. The longer growth stays above 2.75 percent, the more the Reserve Bank is going to be nervous, so to that extent it is important."
"There are always revisions with this, and the other thing we've got to remember is it's a December quarter number, so it's largely historical."
She played down the significance of the upward revision to the September quarter.
"You have to look at the whole annual profile, and that's basically generally flat, which suggests that we are at a turning point as far as economic growth goes."
"The output figure is a negative for the Reserve Bank but on the other side you have higher productivity than most people thought, given those revisions."
"Overall I think it is slightly negative for the market but not overly so."
